commit_message:
Fix various problems to do with segment promotion. Add test file fts4growth2.test, containing tests to check that the FTS index does not grow indefinitely as the table is updated.

fix_commit.message: Fix a signed integer overflow that could occur in fts3 when processing corrupt database records. Bug [bugs:/info/2026-06-11T23:12:25Z | 2026-06-11T23:12:25Z].
fix_commit.author: dan

findings.title: Signed integer overflow in fts3ReadEndBlockField when negating SMALLEST_INT64
findings.message: In fts3ReadEndBlockField(), the code parses a numeric value from the database's end_block field into iVal, then computes *pnByte = (iVal * (i64)iMul). When iMul is -1 (set when the text contains a '-' sign) and iVal holds the value SMALLEST_INT64 (INT64_MIN = -9223372036854775808), the multiplication SMALLEST_INT64 * -1 causes a signed integer overflow — undefined behavior in C. A corrupt database record containing the string '-9223372036854775808' as the end_block field triggers this path. The fix adds a guard: if( (i64)iVal==SMALLEST_INT64 ) iMul = 1; to avoid the overflow, treating the record as corrupt.
findings.suggestion: Before computing *pnByte = (iVal * (i64)iMul), check if iVal equals SMALLEST_INT64 and if so, set iMul = 1 to prevent negating INT64_MIN. The record is already known to be corrupt at this point, so the exact value does not matter — only avoiding undefined behavior does.

ground_truth.root_cause: The fts3ReadEndBlockField() function parses a decimal integer with an optional leading '-' from the database's end_block field. It stores the magnitude in iVal and tracks the sign in iMul. The final result *pnByte = (iVal * (i64)iMul) does not guard against the edge case where iVal == SMALLEST_INT64 (INT64_MIN) and iMul == -1. Because -INT64_MIN cannot be represented as a signed 64-bit integer, this multiplication is undefined behavior per the C standard. This pattern was introduced in 2014 when the iMul sign-handling logic was first added.
